description: A focused information pack for systemic lupus erythematosus (lupus), its symptoms, diagnosis, treatment research and life with the condition. It is an information-discovery aid, not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Systemic lupus erythematosus (lupus) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, causing inflammation that can affect several organs.
synopsis.manifestations: Symptoms vary and may come and go in flares and periods of lower activity. Common features include fatigue, joint pain or swelling, fever and skin rashes or sensitivity to sunlight; inflammation may also involve the kidneys, blood, heart, lungs or nervous system.
synopsis.management: Clinicians assess symptoms, examination findings and laboratory results, sometimes with imaging or a biopsy. Care is individualised and may include medicines such as hydroxychloroquine, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants or biologic treatments, with monitoring for organ involvement and treatment effects.
synopsis.outlook: Lupus has a variable course. Many people manage it with ongoing specialist care, while flares and organ involvement can require changes in treatment; outlook depends on the organs affected, disease activity and response to care.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered studies involving lupus, including medicines, biologics, monitoring and approaches to organ involvement. A listing is not a recommendation or a statement about eligibility.

termDefinitions.lupus clinical trial: A planned study involving people that evaluates an intervention or approach for lupus under a defined protocol.
termDefinitions.SLE clinical trial: A clinical trial focused on systemic lupus erythematosus.
termDefinitions.trial participant: A person who takes part in a clinical study.
termDefinitions.study recruitment: The process of identifying and enrolling people who may take part in a study.
termDefinitions.investigational: Being studied and not yet established or approved for the use being investigated.
termDefinitions.trial results: Findings reported after researchers analyse information collected during a clinical trial.

topics.heading: Treatment and care
topics.description: Information about lupus medicines, monitoring, flare management and specialist care, presented for education rather than personal treatment decisions.

termDefinitions.hydroxychloroquine: A medicine used in many lupus treatment plans; suitability and monitoring are determined by a clinician.
termDefinitions.corticosteroid: An anti-inflammatory medicine that may be used for some lupus manifestations.
termDefinitions.immunosuppressant: A medicine that reduces selected immune activity and may be used when lupus requires it.
termDefinitions.biologic therapy: A treatment made using biological components that targets particular immune pathways.
termDefinitions.lupus nephritis treatment: Care directed at kidney inflammation caused by lupus, guided by specialist assessment.
termDefinitions.lupus flare: A period when lupus symptoms or inflammation become more active.
termDefinitions.disease activity: A clinical assessment of how active lupus is at a particular time.

topics.heading: Lupus research
topics.description: Research into immune mechanisms, biomarkers, treatments, organ involvement, prevention and outcomes in lupus.

termDefinitions.lupus biomarker: A measurable feature that may help study lupus activity, cause, prognosis or response to treatment.
termDefinitions.lupus outcomes: Measures describing disease activity, organ health, function, wellbeing or other research results.
termDefinitions.precision medicine: An approach that considers individual differences when studying prevention or treatment.

topics.heading: Causes, genetics and diagnosis
topics.description: How inherited and environmental factors, immune markers, examinations and tests help researchers and clinicians understand lupus.

termDefinitions.lupus genetics: The study of inherited and newly occurring genetic variation that may influence lupus risk or features.
termDefinitions.antinuclear antibody: An antibody directed against structures in a cell nucleus; ANA results are interpreted with symptoms and other findings.
termDefinitions.ANA test: A blood test that detects antinuclear antibodies; a positive result alone does not diagnose lupus.
termDefinitions.anti-dsDNA: An autoantibody that can be found in some people with lupus and is interpreted in clinical context.
termDefinitions.lupus diagnosis: The clinical process of evaluating symptoms, examination and test results because no single test diagnoses lupus.
termDefinitions.autoantibody: An antibody that reacts with the body's own tissues or components.

topics.heading: Living with lupus
topics.description: Daily life, wellbeing, work, relationships, activity, sun protection and self-management alongside clinical care for lupus.

termDefinitions.living with lupus: Managing everyday life and wellbeing while living with lupus.
termDefinitions.lupus quality of life: The physical, emotional, social and practical effects of lupus and its treatment on daily life.
termDefinitions.lupus fatigue: Tiredness that may occur with lupus or other factors and should be discussed with a clinician when persistent.
termDefinitions.lupus and pregnancy: Information about pregnancy planning and care when lupus is present; advice is individual and specialist-led.
termDefinitions.photosensitivity: Increased sensitivity to light, which can be a feature of some lupus rashes.

topics.heading: Caregiving and support
topics.description: Information for family members, care partners and support networks, including communication, practical help and community support.

termDefinitions.lupus caregiver: A person who provides practical, personal or emotional support to someone with lupus.
termDefinitions.lupus support group: People affected by lupus who meet or communicate to exchange information and support.
termDefinitions.care coordination: Organising communication and services among the people and teams involved in someone's care.
termDefinitions.peer support: Support exchanged between people with shared experience of lupus.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Public understanding, stigma reduction, access to rheumatology care, disability rights, education, community organisations and research funding.

termDefinitions.lupus advocacy: Speaking or acting to improve lupus awareness, rights, services, policy or research.
termDefinitions.lupus awareness: Efforts to improve public understanding of lupus and the experiences of people affected.
termDefinitions.lupus access: The availability and affordability of appropriate lupus information, assessment, treatment and support.
termDefinitions.lupus stigma: Negative stereotypes, misunderstanding or discrimination directed at people because of lupus.
